# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document is a companion to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the RFC’s stage sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> The stage order and acceptance gates are governed exclusively by the main text of RFC-039. This
> document is responsible only for decomposing the work into an executable granularity and
> registering conflicts that have not yet been adjudicated.

## Position and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Stages, in one-to-one correspondence with the stage sequence of RFC-039                               |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by stage, each of which can be staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 268         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                           |

**Reserved numbering gaps (not reclaimed)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the
LALRPOP route was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). All three
have had no corresponding entries since the WBS was established—the full history of this document
has zero matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can be used for verification),
and the repository contains no references to them. `8.1` corresponds precisely to stage 1 of `05`
(test resurrection and completion): that stage has been split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so
P8’s numbering is aligned with its stage numbers (stage 0 → `8.0`, stage 2 → `8.2`, and so on).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependency relationships, parallelization groups,
and binding of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for the tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the
rationale for the stage order (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: every newly registered level-2/level-3 row
**must contain two fields**—“**Owning stage**” (the P stage to which it genuinely belongs, which may
differ from its current section) and “**Blocks the mainline**”. `Registered, awaiting scheduling` is
no longer the default state; an unmarked item is considered **not schedulable**. Numbering must be
**unique across the entire document** (cross-track tasks use a track number, such as `029g.x`, and
must not occupy `N.x`).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: checked rows contain only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number, when one exists—on a
single line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching completion items** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not
record the fix, the criterion chain, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions**: those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a board,
not a process chronicle. **Do not record adjudication labels or restate conclusions**: “user
adjudication A/B/C,” “Proposal A,” “Approach A,” and “the final implementation is…” must not appear
in this table. The board answers only “Is it complete?”; consult the commit message and the RFC-039
adjudication register for decisions and outcomes.

**Short hashes are based on the post-push state**: a closure row records the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push has completed. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then
write the closure row** (see “Commit hashes are obtained after push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closure commit itself has no hash—self-reference
is impossible.

**The count columns contain numbers only**: the level-1/2/3 counts under “Position and Scope”
contain only the current values; incremental history such as `+1 = …` does not appear in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While aggregating the “implementation points” from eight documents into this table, **five hard gaps
in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Resolution                                                                                                                                    |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC-039 defines P5 (checker decomposition) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but not one of the seven documents contains a section describing how the decomposition is to be performed; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains a single mention of `annotations.rs`, the only reference in the entire batch.                                                                                 | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below).                                                                                       |
| G2  | **The three `include!` conversions have conflicting ownership and no implementation**. RFC-039 lists them under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; and S7 of `06` also lists them. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) does **not** include `semantic_tokens.rs`.                                                                                                                                                         | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC-039 and `06` now point here.  |
| G3  | **Three concurrent lists of CI scripts exist**. RFC-039 lists four `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists four scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists four different checks under entirely different names; and `04` previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (this script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` has dual ownership under P4 and P9. | The unified list appears in §P9 of this document (10 active scripts, each owned by one stage); all other documents refer to this table.       |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that must be resurrected,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with” the `Precedence` enum; `05` advocates deletion.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | **Resurrect in P1, retain in P8** (decision record C1; Pratt is no longer to be removed).                                                     |
| G5  | **Conflicting wording for the L2 objective**: RFC-039 and the index of this directory previously said “grammar-driven syntax.”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | It has converged on a **declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3. |

## Target Design: Stage Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (do not invent; do not pad endlessly; do not
patch when a refactoring is called for) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be
established before work begins; otherwise, while resurrecting tests in P1, work will already be
adding `mod` declarations to `tests/mod.rs`—precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Defects (Minimal Approach)

Source: the defect-fix half of [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3 ＋ **2026-10-07
silent-discard-point audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, adjudicated 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a later stage
> discovers a defect for which the “old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack exhaustion, or silently
> returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed in passing during the refactoring**, but all four
> requirements are mandatory: ① red before green (the red criterion must exist first and actually
> fail); ② do not change the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled
> successfully and ran correctly” (they must not become failures, and their existing diagnostic
> codes/text/exit codes must not be changed or removed); ③ record in the same commit (this row
> identifies the error type + the stage’s revision note + the mandatory “Error type” line in the PR
> block); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff. **D user-visible
> semantics / E external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must still be adjudicated
> first. See [07 §Routing Criteria for Semantic Corrections](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the
> expanded criteria and A–F whitelist; do not accept “default super-refactoring + ex-post
> registration”** (reason: RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, fixes and regressions cannot be
> distinguished, and this conflicts with both “there is no C5′” and “no relaxation whatsoever”).

**Acceptance**: the defect criterion turns green, and **deliberately removing the fix must turn it
red again**. **Risk**: the new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is forbidden);
3.4.3 requires manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 follow the C2/C3 criteria and the P9 9.2 gate. **Risk**:
the new diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized corpus-differential
baseline and CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding channel**: P3 does not have to wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites
> for 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, performance
> baseline) may proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding for correctness defects (such as
> `Sorted(3)` passing silently) must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure work. 3.3 (convert
> panic to diagnostic) has no prerequisite and may land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (external track / #399 — ordering constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactoring itself; it is a specification-compliance removal forced by
an ordering constraint.** It is distinct from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (Rust’s
`pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why it must be completed before P4**: 029g’s removal surface overlaps with the rewrite surface of
all four refactoring stages; reversing the order means redoing the same removals and baseline
updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 AST dead variants** + P8 + D1 directory rename (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the pub branch of `collect_exports`         | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!`→real `mod` and checker decomposition are **pure moves**, and the pub branch is moved unchanged into the new files)                                                                                                                                              |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside the body of `check_project`)                     | **P4 4.2.2** (slim down `check_project`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `semantic_tokens`’s `Public` modifier                               | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

**Acceptance (behavioral changes, red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavioral changes must have a red criterion before code is
   changed—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② an unreferenced top-level
   binding in Lib/Script roles newly reports W1001 (previously pub items were absolutely exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` case from
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, equivalent new cases must replace
   them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ the
   corpus-differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG are updated in
   the same commit; the IR snapshot is expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff must be
   explained.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other stages (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: overlaps with 3.4 files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must run serially
and must not run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; the implementer chooses which to do first according to the context at hand.

> **Commit cross-reference (2026-10-08)**: this section’s incorporation (the P3.5 section +
> main-chain/constraint row) and RFC-039’s D56 were incorporated together into `97071c81b` during
> the parallel-stream workspace cleanup—the commit message records “3.4 supplementary registration +
> D57/D58 adjudication filing” and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten; following
> the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 landing note), it is recorded in
> place as a basis for subsequent binary search.

a **test-only constant**, and production code must not depend on it; **zero behavioral change** (only comments change; 4.4.2’s acceptance number is unchanged; issue |                                            | 4.9.9 A cross-unit single-definition method called with **named arguments** loses the formal-parameter name table (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during the 7c closure period): calling a cross-unit method (injected through the registry) with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, and named-argument calls within a single file work normally. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` contains `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, whereas `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Class C** (the old behavior was unsuccessful: named arguments were silently dropped, followed by runtime failure or a silent wrong value). **Scope (final form after two narrowing rounds on 2026-11-26—only three additions; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—obtains the declaration-time formal names from the unique cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads`, keyed by the defining unit’s qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` (candidate ↔ mixed-compilation IR name ↔ formal-name triplets are in the same order, using the same source as the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses `method_dispatch_name`’s qualified name to look up the name table rather than two separate bare names. These two locations fix only **bare-name imports** (`local == target`) for cross-unit methods: the candidate injection surface retains the pre-4.9.9 narrowing rule (skip when `local != target`), so named arguments for alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges in **ascending module-key order**—**Class C (independent of the original bug): eliminate “the same input produces multiple results” caused by HashMap iteration order**, not the original bug’s fix; criterion = the same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders; only one single binding is permitted for the same method key; removing ascending-order merge produces two results). **Criterion (red before green)**: 2 driver-level tests in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (bare import with one candidate: 6.0 / two candidates selected by name: 6.0 and 30, both with value assertions; the file header records the medical-history gate); unit test in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (the `method_param_info` empty-name-table guard ⇒ None; positive control returns a non-empty table unchanged); unit test in `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the deterministic criterion listed above). Project-level fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (the `alias-overload` fixture is deleted together with retirement of the alias surface); the corpus-differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` now has 404 lines: **relative to the direct parent commit `ac810e97`, 405→404** (the intermediate state contained `alias-overload`); **relative to the pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 basic fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`; `alias-overload` did not enter the final history). The line-count change = an inevitable result of fixtures entering and leaving (after `corpus_probe` regeneration, it is byte-for-byte identical to the committed baseline), **not lost coverage**. **Known gaps (each named explicitly; old behavior = silently ignored or silently discarded; D60② should report but does not, Class A)**: closure-value binding / block-body function declarations / named nested function declarations / built-in container constructors other than `len` named arguments / whole-module imports / the RFC-004 binding arm. **Two points have been corrected based on P0 measurement**: ① **static-function forms** (both intra-unit and cross-unit, definition and binding forms) are **entirely unavailable today**—the intra-unit `check` reports E3006, the cross-unit definition-form `run` reports E6007, and the cross-unit binding-form `run` reports E6006; positional and named arguments produce the same code, so this is unrelated to named arguments and is not “named arguments are silently discarded”; ② **cross-unit RFC-004 positional arguments also fail** (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006); the root cause is that the dispatch name is absent from the merged function table, again unrelated to named arguments. **Fixed (4.9.10-S2b, D59 Class A in-passing fix: old behavior E6007/E1014 was unsuccessful, so no previously successful program becomes a failure)**: ① **alias-import named arguments** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② **namespace arms** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (the receiver type is inferred and has no written annotation). These three previously produced runtime E6007 with silent argument loss or check-time false rejection with `E1014 (available: )`; all now fill slots by declaration-time formal name (value assertion 6.0; criterion `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs`, with the red state recorded in that file’s header medical-history gate). Two identity-surface residuals remain, one of which has been closed: an intra-unit same-named type + alias import (two same-named definition-side identities coexist, and the import surface cannot register the local declaration) **has been closed with the 4.9.10-S2a import-surface convergence** (the project fixture `same-name-type-local-and-alias-import` is fully green); For same-named types across modules, three consumers—the candidate injection (`driver::arms::visible_method_overloads`), typecheck’s formal-name/candidate matching, and IR dispatch (`method_dispatch_name`)—independently guess the provider by name, so changing any one of them moves the “silent wrong value” to another location. **Root-cause solution**: upgrade type identity to **module-qualified identity** (`{module}.{Type}`), and change the method-candidate key accordingly to `{module}.{Type}.{method}`; one resolver produces the identity and the three consumers only read it. This changes the shape of `overload_resolutions` keys and mixed-compilation names and is D59 **Class D** (requires adjudication). **Disposition in this round (after two narrowing rounds from 4.9.9)**: 4.9.9 **introduces no new rejection**—the previous six rounds’ Class D rejection list (all named arguments rejected with E1014 / positional-argument conflict forms always rejected with E1107 / the E5006 ambiguity prohibition at the import-name resolution point) is deleted with the mechanism and all entries are voided; the `len` form is normal). **Three items closed with this round**: ① method-candidate key / method key changed to module-qualified `{module}.{Type}.{method}` (L0’s dual `DefPath` representation + S2a’s table key and single-point resolution; **Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is migrated with the annotation family in the future, **then** `checker.rs` must
add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged; measurement
shows that 5.3 did **not** migrate it, so this batch adds no re-export (the criterion was already
satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules of merely 200–400 lines—this increases
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields no decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split when the files grow back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62’s end state is a **unified term world**—type positions and value positions share
> one set of compile-time terms. A strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** for slot allocation, and the call-site argument view and
> implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a **pure
> determination** (the two sides are equal after normalization; type variables are not bound);
> evidence is the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value
> environment/single-value pinning/Γ equality); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (both
> closed terms and open terms/recursion hold); Σ construction sites **reuse the same evidence
> interface** rather than creating another one. **Completion criterion = the invariants hold, not
> that all substage names have been completed.**

> **6.9 closure criterion**: I1–I5 and I7 all hold; I6 is closed according to the design-review
> conclusion for 6.9.5 (does not block P7); every I8 slice has evidence; the residual items
> #537/#539/#540/#541/#542/#552 all have a disposition (fixed/explicitly excluded/separate item);
> #542 was implemented on 2026-11-19. **Do not substitute “all substages checked off” for the
> invariants holding.**

> **Partial order (not a serial chain)**: A facts → {A.C3, B.d, C.2, D design}; B kernel → {B.d,
> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 adjudication → A.C3;
> determination-point protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in
> parallel but require file-surface coordination (C3 leans typecheck→mono, while d leans
> types/solver→sema); C.2 may run in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (it does not depend on
> defeq); D implementation waits for confirmation of the B design package and depends on A (q=0
> erasure) and C.1 (dispatch), and may depend on 6.9.3’s typed exit. **P7 gate = exits of A/B/C; D
> does not block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 adjudication (A adjudicated on 2026-11-16; measurement)**: the old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been
> deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request is
> created, and the representation layer’s `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold `k-1`.
> **The adjudication has changed to two orthogonal decisions + one terminating subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: do not
> specialize); D-b evaluation point (only mono is possible; C-1’s second field and C-2
> reconstruction from IR both break the single representation/evaluator, so C-3 = A); **F4-T
> termination** (naive firing causes the recursive chain to hit `max_depth` and E3005; T-a:
> conditionally fire within the instance / T-b: bounded firing + fall back to the original at the
> boundary / T-c: termination layer or specification change). **First perform the measurement, then
> adjudicate; before measurement, “A is implementable” must not be treated as a conclusion.** **User
> (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task, and
> full realization of I4 is not claimed.**

> **B.d prerequisite: determination-point protocol (not yet written)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies that
> “determination points first use unification; after unification fails, defeq may be used, but all
> partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled back.” The
> implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new
> `decide` layer; may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (no unbound variables);
> what are the snapshot/restoration boundary and cost; and do unify and defeq share one budget or
> have separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for
> subtyping/Any/Never; defeq determines equivalence only and does not take over subtyping;
> bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **First provide the
> protocol and production call graph, then write code**; 6.9.3c’s wiring contract wasted two rounds
> because it assumed `can_assign` was the determination point, while `AssignmentChecker` has zero
> production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ error-code generator idempotence (if an emission point/code table is
> changed); ④ behavioral changes classified under D59 and implemented red before green. **Wiring
> tasks additionally require**: production call-graph evidence (the production entry point, number
> of paths, and which are reachable); unit-test reachability must not be passed off as user
> reachability; rollback and budget must have measured numbers. **Residual disposition**: #537
> (Class D, silent discard of proof-function formal-parameter refinement; do not fix before
> adjudication, and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; C-stage
> boundary, and until closed, 6.9.4 covers only intra-module code), #540 (deep-nesting stack
> explosion; **closed**—3.20.30 closed on 2026-11-14: a 64MB large-stack thread at the orchestration
> layer + parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019; see the 3.20.30 row in `09`), #541
> (TailCall; **closed**—three sites changed together on 2026-11-16: `call_form_is_rewritten` /
> `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` cover `Call`/`TailCall` through the
> single-point `rewritten_call_target`, and init sections and function bodies share one
> site-rewriting implementation; red→green + three mutations), #542 (orphaned shared layer;
> **implemented (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono two entry-point connections + removal of the
> temporary C2c avoidance; red→green, 402/402, function-table attribution and deviations), #552
> (proof execution for imported multi-parameter predicates; adjacent to 6.9.5, separate item).
> **Ownership awaiting adjudication**: the four open-constraint tripwires in
> `rfc027_refined_transparency` (`Eq(N, n)`) do not belong to 6.9.4’s constant-equality bridge;
> decide whether they remain in 6.9.4’s outOfScope or are reassigned to 6.9.1/E4018’s proof-function
> surface.

> **Non-claims/boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim that Π/Σ is fully realized; 6.9.4 covers only constant equalities
> and does not fulfill the `Eq(N,n)` open-constraint tripwire; the second value position of
> `f(y)(y)` is outside this item; witness erasure ≠ runtime-check erasure; if #537 is not fixed,
> 6.9.4/6.9.5 cover only forms that do not depend on proof-function formal-parameter refinement; if
> #539 is not fixed, 6.9.4 covers only intra-module code; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 is
> implemented (2026-11-19); 2.1.4’s inner-isolation red state was cleared on 2026-11-20 (the
> criterion was rewritten around slot identity at the 2.1.4 closure) ⇒ all prerequisites for
> promoting `verify` to a gate are removed.

**Hard acceptance** (**2026-10-27 revised baseline, following the 2026-10-26 decision ②**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be empty in **each round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive changed code, such
as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required by the change, but
each modification must be recorded with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be deleted
and assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new
diagnostic codes + baseline updates), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
handled as a separate round with separate adjudication.

> **Revision relationship**: the original baseline (2026-10-26 decision ②) was written as
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying a blanket zero-diff requirement to the entire `tests/`
> directory; the revised baseline **only changes direct-drive test files from “zero diff” to “may be
> changed but must record file / line count / reason”**, while the **zero-diff requirement for the
> corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard library
> (`src/std/`) remains unchanged**. First application = 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs`
> changed, with **3 lines** (2 occurrences of `assert_format_eq` changed from `i64`→`Int64` + 1
> comment line), reason = the expected type name in the assertion must be synchronized with the

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority; missing a consumer silently changes
associativity (no error, only a changed parse result). The defenses are the permanent D1–D3
assertions and operator-property cross-check tests; a new operator must simultaneously enter the
table and the cross-check test.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on D0/D2 from `08`**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or action
> code refers backward to `sema`, it will be blocked by `check-boundary.py`.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding channel (adjudicated 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (the multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) may proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding for correctness defects must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure work; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver
> requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| P1 → P2                   | Resurrecting tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Defect criteria must be written **red first**—2.4.1/2.4.3 and the multi-file corpus layer 2.3.2 must exist so that the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order causes bugs to be固化 as “established behavior” in the stage table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)’s removal surface overlaps the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list appears in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means redoing the same removals on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` conversion and checker decomposition modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise regressions cannot be located through binary search                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations are not converged first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; **P7 gate = exits of 6.9 stages A/B/C** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completion of 6.9.4), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume the quantifier-derived views and defeq interface, but must not create a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite, is not subject to this gate, and must not consume undecided defeq/quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | 9.5’s snapshot baseline and 9.3’s `pub(crate)` leak count can take their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

### Parallelizable Groups

| Group                                  | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only one authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | The file sets are disjoint: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs. `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                     |
| B                                      | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| C                                      | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| D                                      | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 track                                    | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                               |
| E                                      | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | None depends on the others after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| F                                      | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced by P0 may be developed in parallel) | 9.5’s snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| G                                      | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | The file sets are disjoint (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` sites in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pair overlaps) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5 in
the same batch of files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s pub-removal batch and the silent-channel
fix must run serially).

**New internal document constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is P7’s pure-move prerequisite), and 7b’s `Phi` arm must precede
7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is established as an independent stage rather than merged into P9**—gates are “post-hoc
  checks,” while rules are “pre-hoc judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “a patch was applied when
  a refactoring was called for”; only the D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the original G3 gap with three concurrent
  lists made closure impossible. This table merges them, with 10 active scripts each owned by one
  stage (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24); report-only status and hard-mode transition
  points are explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to be done after the
  refactoring”**—its removal surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactoring means redoing the same removals on the new grammar, new
  checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and RFC
  status corrections into S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding checker decomposition would exceed the independently revertible
  granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as hard acceptance**—the decomposition must be independently
  revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “the fixed defects
  should not be rolled back,” but does not require a record of what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: every 1.3.x fix commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect
  description as a basis for subsequent binary search.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b, two
  exclusive commits, per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 reference renames; missing one **silently
  changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was incorporated into 7e.1, and the
  deletion action landed in P10 S6.1 (6753bbe).
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned “independent issues”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: `2341` was incorporated into 7e.3; `2315` was rechecked on 2026-11-28 and
  found to be an audit false positive (the field has no producer, and the language layer has no
  throw/try/catch), 7e.2 was cancelled, and the exception remnants were deleted by P10 S6.1
  (6753bbe).
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no stage ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into the generation-time gate task in P10 S6.2 and implemented (a2e570c).

## Conflict Register: All Conflicts Have Been Adjudicated

> **The original “conflict register” C1–C8 and the open questions in each document have all
> converged into [the RFC-039 decision register](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md)
> (D1–D50).** This document contains no pending items. The item-by-item mapping is:

| Original number | Issue                                                                               | Decision                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| C1              | `precedence_inline.rs` is resurrected in P1 and deleted in P8                       | **Resurrect** (the P1 prerequisite is that resurrection includes real assertions); P8 no longer deletes the file (Pratt is retained)                                                 |
| C2              | “Grammar-driven” commitment vs. table-based implementation                          | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + a single declarative precedence table + two `BinOp` sets cross-checked from the same source (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn); see P8 8.3       |
| C3              | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification                   | **S1 is classified under C6** (resurrection does not require an equivalence criterion, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure resurrection” |
| C4              | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` whitelist                                        | **No whitelist**; the difference set must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                                    |
| C5              | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions have not been verified | **P4’s 4.2.7 lists this as a mandatory verification item**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                                                       |
| C6              | The wasm playground fix requires P4’s `ProgramKind`                                 | The wasm-path defect fix is incorporated into 4.2.8; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                                   |
| C7              | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                                  | **Assigned to 04** (P7 batch c); see D21                                                                                                                                             |
| C8              | Correction of `upvalue_count` and the `.42` version number                          | **Fix + raise `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`); see D17                                               |
